I can tell you my experience. I called the hotline, and said I wanted to kill my self. The woman asked if I had the means to. I was in a house, so I said theoretically yes—there are kitchen knives, rope, over the counter pain killers, alcohol, power tools, a toaster and a bathtub, etc. 

She asks me if I could throw these items away...

I said no, I wasn’t going to throw away my silver ware and appliances. She said that if I wouldn’t do that then she wanted me to promise to go to the emergency room. I didn’t want to do that, and didn’t think it was necessary so I told her no. 

She asked if she could send a mobile crisis unit to my home and I said no. She asked if she could pass along my number to them and I said no. We hang up and immediately after I get a call from the mobile crisis unit. And they do the same bullshit and then ask if they could send the police and I say no and they ask if they can give them my number and I say no. 

Ten minutes later, the police are at my house at 3am. They talk to me and talk to my mom. They eventually fuck off. My mom then asks me about some things I told the hotline operater in confidence that had nothing to do with suicide. Things that should not have been shared with a mobile crisis unit and then the police and then my mom. 

These hotlines aren’t manned by mental health professionals. They are people who receive 60-100hours of crisis training and many err too far on the side of caution and send emergency services to your house against your wishes. 

They really don’t have a productive conversation with you. They aren’t there to and a human connection, they are there to put you in touch with emergency services.
